chunks: The Pharaoh said: "O nobles, I am not aware of any other lord of yours but myself. So, O Haman, fire some clay (bricks) to build a tower for me that I may mount up (and see) the God of Moses; for I think he is a liar."
ai.seo_question: What did Pharaoh command Haman to build and why?
ai.summary: In this verse, Pharaoh commands his vizier Haman to construct a 'Sarth' (tower) from baked clay, reflecting the historical Shia scholarly view that this structure served as a physical manifestation of his arrogance and a means to challenge the heavens. This declaration of 'I am your supreme god' underscores the theme of *Tawhid* versus *Taghut*, while his assertion that Moses is a liar highlights the persistent denial of prophetic truth by tyrannical rulers throughout history.
